react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent enrichment paradigms converged on galactose-related carbon metabolism as the dominant biological signal. RaMP-ORA ranked Galactose Metabolism (SMPDB:SMP00043) and Galactosemia (SMPDB:SMP00182) as the top two hits with FDR = 4.25×10⁻¹¹, driven by four metabolites (sucrose, myo-inositol, galactinol, glycerol) out of 31 pathway members, giving a fold-enrichment of 1162. A second ORA run also identified Glycerophospholipid biosynthesis (REACT:R-HSA-1483206, FDR = 4.21×10⁻⁴) with myo-inositol and glycerol as hits. The m/z-direct method mummichog independently ranked Galactose metabolism (MUMM:galactose_metabolism, p = 5.88×10⁻⁴) fourth overall, overlapping six of the seven input metabolites (fructose 1-phosphate, sucrose, glycerol, myo-inositol, galactinol, D-glucose) against a pathway of 13 members — the highest overlap density of any pathway in that result. Deoxycytidine (C00881) did not map to galactose metabolism in any tool and appears to be a peripheral or off-pathway hit, consistent with its absence from the leading galactose pathway hits. The convergence of ORA and mummichog on galactose metabolism with six shared input compounds establishes this pathway as the primary affected system; glycerophospholipid metabolism is a secondary, inositol/glycerol-mediated signal. Galactinol (KEGG:C01235), the galactosyl-donor substrate in galactose metabolism, is a structurally specific driver that anchors the finding to raffinose-family oligosaccharide biochemistry.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent enrichment paradigms converged on galactose-related carbon metabolism as the dominant biological signal. RaMP-ORA ranked Galactose Metabolism (SMPDB:SMP00043) and Galactosemia (SMPDB:SMP00182) as the top two hits with FDR = 4.25×10⁻¹¹, driven by four metabolites (sucrose, myo-inositol, galactinol, glycerol) out of 31 pathway members, giving a fold-enrichment of 1162. A second ORA run also identified Glycerophospholipid biosynthesis (REACT:R-HSA-1483206, FDR = 4.21×10⁻⁴) with myo-inositol and glycerol as hits. The m/z-direct method mummichog independently ranked Galactose metabolism (MUMM:galactose_metabolism, p = 5.88×10⁻⁴) fourth overall, overlapping six of the seven input metabolites (fructose 1-phosphate, sucrose, glycerol, myo-inositol, galactinol, D-glucose) against a pathway of 13 members — the highest overlap density of any pathway in that result. Deoxycytidine (C00881) did not map to galactose metabolism in any tool and appears to be a peripheral or off-pathway hit, consistent with its absence from the leading galactose pathway hits. The convergence of ORA and mummichog on galactose metabolism with six shared input compounds establishes this pathway as the primary affected system; glycerophospholipid metabolism is a secondary, inositol/glycerol-mediated signal. Galactinol (KEGG:C01235), the galactosyl-donor substrate in galactose metabolism, is a structurally specific driver that anchors the finding to raffinose-family oligosaccharide biochemistry.
